doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Matching family names and Teddie's birthplace near Charleston
summary: Hank's father was Henry William and Teddie's William Henry; Teddie describes her father's role in a small South Carolina town.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Share with us some of the things that you talked with us about last night period he were talking about the similarities between your two families. You were talking about your dad…

About the similarities. Remember how there were 10 in your family and they were 10 at one time in my family and so forth? My father's name was Henry William and your father's name was William Henry? Her father's name was Henry. My father's name was Henry William.
It coincidence with the William Henry and the Henry William.
When you found that out what did that make you think? Did you notice the coincidence at the time?

Just recently I noticed the coordination of the names, the Henry Williams and William Henry. I said, “I’ve never noticed that my father fell into that Henry Williams to." He said, "he is William Henry." I used to call him uncle Bill and he would say, "Well, good night pop." (Inaudible) that I was born in.
Your birthplace. Tell them your birthplace.

My birthplace? I was born…The beginning of it was my grandfather had a whole lot to do with my father settling their because it was bought by a Baptist Minister. It was a funny thing. The whole town was bought. But, they were still the South Carolina that had appointed a different law estate. They would work with the smaller communities. Charleston, I guess you know of Charleston South Carolina?

This was only 22 miles above Charleston. So, one time they were so upset about my father closing the town hall and not letting the children go to the school library because they had promised him a new school for the last five years. He just closed it up and said that he needed to make them account for the taxes. By the time the next year was over, they had a new school. That was the only way that he could deal with them in Charleston.
It was by twisting their arm, you know?

(Laughs) that was the method he used. He said, "if you don't get them in a school, then you're not going to get anything here." He said, “You can blame it on me.” By that time, they were all throwing daggers at him. Now, they’re all throwing kisses at him!
